content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Fragility", "construction": "Using annual 10-K disclosures, compute the fraction of a firm's cost of goods sold attributable to its largest few disclosed suppliers (or, absent explicit disclosure, proxy via inventory turnover volatility combined with segment input dependence). Score firms into deciles by concentration each June and rebalance annually.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on few suppliers face underpriced input-disruption risk; investors underweight this fragility until shocks materialize, so they must be compensated with higher expected returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high supplier concentration"}, {"name": "R&D Acceleration", "construction": "Compute the year-over-year change in R&D-to-sales ratio scaled by its own three-year standard deviation: (RD_t/Sales_t - RD_{t-1}/Sales_{t-1}) / stdev(RD/Sales over 3 years). Form deciles annually using Compustat data lagged six months.", "rationale": "Sharp acceleration in innovation intensity signals management conviction about future growth options that the market is slow to capitalize into prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high R&D acceleration"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Momentum", "construction": "From Compustat item ORDER BACKLOG (data item OB), compute growth in backlog scaled by lagged total assets, then subtract contemporaneous sales growth to isolate unbilled demand buildup. Rank cross-sectionally each fiscal year, lagged four months.", "rationale": "Rising backlog relative to recognized revenue reflects future demand not yet in earnings; the accrual-focused market underreacts to this off-income-statement signal.", "higher_returns_for": "high backlog-minus-sales growth"}, {"name": "Advertising-to-Market Cap Value Tilt", "construction": "Divide annual advertising expense (Compustat XAD) by market capitalization at fiscal year end. Form deciles among firms with nonzero advertising, rebalanced each June.", "rationale": "Advertising builds intangible brand capital not on the balance sheet; high advertising relative to price indicates understated intangible book value, mimicking a value effect that standard B/M misses.", "higher_returns_for": "high advertising-to-market"}, {"name": "Dispersion in Quarterly Earnings Signs", "construction": "Over the trailing 12 quarters, count the number of sign changes in seasonally-differenced quarterly earnings (positive-to-negative or negative-to-positive). Standardize and rank cross-sectionally each quarter.", "rationale": "Frequent earnings sign reversals proxy for opaque, hard-to-value businesses that carry an information-uncertainty premium demanded by investors.", "higher_returns_for": "high number of sign changes"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Smoothness", "construction": "Compute the coefficient of variation of annual capex-to-assets over the trailing five years. Rank firms into deciles annually with standard accounting lag.", "rationale": "Firms with lumpy, volatile investment face higher real-option and financing risk that is compensated, whereas smooth investors are safer and earn lower returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high capex volatility"}, {"name": "Insider Trading Breadth", "construction": "From SEC Form 4 filings over the trailing six months, compute the net number of distinct insiders buying minus selling, scaled by total number of insiders. Rank monthly.", "rationale": "Broad insider consensus (many distinct insiders buying) conveys more credible private information than concentrated trades by a single officer, and the market underweights the breadth dimension.", "higher_returns_for": "high net insider breadth"}, {"name": "Deferred Revenue Growth", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in deferred/unearned revenue liabilities (Compustat) scaled by lagged total assets. Rank cross-sectionally each fiscal year with a four-month lag.", "rationale": "Growth in customer prepayments signals contracted future revenue and pricing power not yet recognized in earnings; the market underreacts to this liability-side growth signal.", "higher_returns_for": "high deferred revenue growth"}, {"name": "Tax-Book Income Gap Persistence", "construction": "Estimate the gap between book pretax income and taxable income (inferred from current tax expense divided by statutory rate), scaled by assets, and measure its three-year average persistence. Rank annually.", "rationale": "Persistent positive book-tax gaps signal aggressive accruals and lower-quality earnings, so such firms subsequently underperform as reversals occur.", "higher_returns_for": "low persistent book-tax gap"}, {"name": "Geographic Sales Diversification Discount", "construction": "Using segment disclosures, compute a Herfindahl index across geographic revenue segments; higher values mean concentrated domestic sales, lower values mean globally diversified. Rank annually with accounting lag.", "rationale": "Geographically concentrated firms bear undiversified regional demand risk that is underpriced by investors focused on product-market rather than geographic exposure, earning a compensating premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high geographic concentration (Herfindahl)"}]}
